key_insight: A simple “deletions” strategy for carving out atomic environments from large simulations produces the best small-cell inputs for DFT-based training of machine-learning interatomic potentials.
engineering_relevance: This improves how active-learning and on-the-fly potential training can obtain accurate local reference data from very large atomistic simulations without excessive setup complexity.
method: Benchmarked multiple extraction shapes/sizes for embedding local regions into periodic DFT-ready cells.
Compared extraction methods across diverse materials: amorphous SiO2, Ta with screw dislocations, and molten C.
Evaluated whether a passivating envelope is needed and found deletions to be a strong baseline.
evidence_signal: The authors report a benchmark across multiple material classes and state that the deletions method outperforms alternative extraction approaches.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the local defect chemistry and boundary treatment, so extracted cells still need careful validation for each system and target property.
paper_title: Extracting Atomic Environments for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
